title: Regional availability scoring and fallback ranking for inference routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We need a production-ready region selection component that ranks candidate regions and model variants based on recent telemetry so requests are routed to the region that best balances latency SLOs, availability, and cost. Current routing uses a simple static preference + failover. That approach leads to transient degradations when a preferred region shows short-lived p95 spikes or packet-loss bursts.

Goals:
- Compute an availability score per region that combines latency distribution (p50/p95), error-rate, and observed packet loss/network retries.
- Provide a fallback ranking for model variants (e.g., quantized vs full-precision) when a region's score falls below thresholds.
- Support tier-aware routing (premium vs standard customers) with different weightings and SLOs.
- Make scoring transparent and debuggable in the Console with per-region time series and recent decisions.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement autoscaling policies or billing changes. It focuses on the decision layer (scoring + routing policy).

High-level approach:
1) Telemetry aggregation: use the existing metrics pipeline (prometheus / traces) to produce a sliding-window summary for each region: median (p50) and tail (p95) for request-to-first-byte and token-stream latencies, 1m error rate, and network retry count. Window size default = 5m, decayed weighting for older samples.
2) Normalize metrics to a 0-1 scale per region using historical baselines per-region (rolling baseline computed from previous 7 days).
3) Compute weighted availability score S = w_latency*L + w_tail*T + w_errors*E + w_net*N where each term is normalized and weights vary by customer tier. Default weights: standard {0.45,0.35,0.10,0.10}, premium {0.60,0.30,0.05,0.05}.
4) Fallback ranking: when S < threshold (tier-specific), produce an ordered list of alternatives combining: other regions sorted by S, compatible model-variant substitutes (e.g., same checkpoint lower-precision) scored by quality-impact estimate and cost delta.
5) Decision API: expose a deterministic region selector function that returns chosen_region, fallback_list, reason_code, score_breakdown, and telemetry_snapshot used for the decision. This will be used by the router and for Console tracing.

Trade-offs considered:
- Short windows make routing reactive but risk flip-flopping; long windows hide regressions. We chose a decayed 5m window with a minimum holdout (30s) to avoid rapid oscillation.
- Using historical baselines adjusts for regional variance (e.g., APAC baseline different from US), but adds state complexity. We keep baseline computation in the metrics pipeline so the decision layer stays stateless.
- Incorporating model-quality delta in fallback ranking requires offline measurements; we'll bootstrap with model metadata quality penalties and refine with evaluations over time.

Technical design summary:
- Metrics producer: add a small Prometheus job that emits per-region histograms for request latency and counters for error/retries. Already planned in ENG-23800; reuse labels \"region\",\"instance_type\",\"model_variant\".
- Metrics aggregator: create a streaming job (materialized view) that emits normalized metrics every 30s to Redis (or low-latency KV) keyed by region+model_variant. TTL = 10m.
- Scorer service: lightweight stateless service (go) that reads recent snapshot and computes S and fallback list deterministically. Provide a GRPC + HTTP endpoint used by the router. Include feature flags for weight presets.
- Router integration: the runtime router will call scorer with request metadata (customer_tier, model constraints, region hints) and receive routing decision. Router will log decision id and attach to request trace.
- Console: new panel that renders the per-region score time-series, last N decisions, and ability to replay a decision with historical telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- Scorer returns consistent decisions in a unit-tested deterministic way given the same telemetry snapshot.
- End-to-end latency for scoring call < 5ms p95 under expected QPS.
- Router uses scorer decisions for 10% of traffic behind a feature flag; behavior matches expected alternatives in Canary test.
- Console shows per-region score and recent decisions for the past 30 minutes.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement and enable scorer; route 10% of internal traffic via scorer for standard-tier model dev team. Monitor false positives/oscillations for 72h.
- Phase 2: expand to 50% internal + selected customer accounts, enable model-variant fallback suggestions but do not auto-fallback (only suggest).
- Phase 3: enable auto-fallback for standard tier with conservative thresholds; premium tier remains weighted to minimize quality impact.

Experimentation and metrics:
- Key metrics: request latency p50/p95, error-rate, number of region switches per minute (stability), successful auto-fallbacks, customer-facing errors.
- SLO guardrails: if number of region switches > 3/min for a customer, temporarily disable scorer for that customer for 15m.

Dependencies:
- ENG-23800 (metrics histogram job) - metrics pipeline work
- ENG-23301 (router tracing integration) - router needs to attach decision id to traces
- PM-482 (console design for routing panel) - design assets for Console

Links:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Regional+Availability+Scoring (design spec draft)
- Draft PR for scorer skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4892 (WIP)
technical_design_summary: Scorer is stateless; normalized metrics come from metrics materialization. Deterministic scoring formula with tier presets and fallbacks. Expose GRPC + HTTP. Store short-lived snapshots in low-latency KV with TTL. Feature-flag rollout and canary routing. Console panel for observability.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic output for identical telemetry snapshots
Scoring RPC p95 < 5ms under expected load
10% canary routing for internal traffic with no customer impact
Console shows last 30m of scores and decisions
